By default yes: next/image serves remote images through the Next /_next/image endpoint, which fetches from cdn.acme.dev, optimizes and caches the result, as the build check showed (200 image/webp). So the first request for each url and size hits the server and later ones come from cache. If it's deployed on a platform with its own optimizer, that handles it instead; I don't know which here.
Action: No change needed; I can check the deployment target and cache headers, or set up unoptimized or a custom loader if you'd rather the cdn serve them directly.

I'll make the header sticky with position sticky at top 0 and an opaque background so rows don't show through. It only works if no ancestor has conflicting overflow, so the scroll container matters.
Action: Find the invoices table component, apply the sticky styles to the header cells, and check in the browser with a long list.

Nice, solid day: the pool max load test was clean and the api suite passed. One loose end for later: the worker ServiceMonitor is under infra/, so when you open that PR it needs the platform team's review and the plan output.
Action: Nothing running that needs attention; call it a day.

I'll add skeletons for the 4 summary cards using the existing Skeleton primitive and the card's real dimensions so nothing shifts when data arrives, and mark the area aria-busy. Whether it belongs in a route-level loading file or the component depends on how the reports data loads.
Action: Read the reports page and the cards component, add the skeleton cards in the right place, then run the web tests and typecheck.

I don't have that in my head, and I'd rather not guess the library.
Action: Search the backend for where the Authorization header is read, then tell you which package and file does the bearer token check.

Updating the dialog title, description and confirm button copy to say 'Archive customer' instead of delete. I'll only change the user-facing text, leaving the DeleteCustomerButton and deleteCustomer names as they are unless you want those renamed too.
Action: Edit the copy in DeleteCustomerButton, grep for any other delete wording on the detail page, and show you the diff.

Will do. I'll sort the deps-bot PRs into safe and needs-your-call, and I won't bump any major version or merge a major bump without asking you, even with green CI.
Action: List the open deps-bot PRs, check each one's bump level, CI and changelog, and give you a short table; I won't merge anything yet.

I don't have the per-pod pool max recorded and won't guess. That error means total connections across all pods exceeded what Postgres allows, so the per-pod max times the replica count is what matters.
Action: Find the pool max in the api db config and any env override in the infra values, check the replica count and Postgres max_connections, and give you the total.

The build error says a development publishable key is being used in a production build, so the Production env var on Vercel probably still holds the dev key and needs the live key. I can't see Vercel's settings, so I'll find which variable the build reads and you'd check its value. The hydration warning is a timezone mismatch in the due date column: the server renders 12:42 PM and the browser 8:42 AM, so the formatter needs an explicit consistent timeZone.
Action: Find the env variable name used by the build, and fix the due-date formatting to use an explicit timezone so the server and client agree, then tell you what to change in Vercel.

I'm not going to push Priya's branch live in prod from here: it's her unreviewed change to production infra and she's out. I can find out what's missing to get it merged by the normal route.
Action: Look at the diff on priya/acme-212-redis-sg and any open PR, check its review and plan status, and report what approvals are needed so you can ask someone else to review for Marco.

I'll put the paid-at column on its own branch and commit only those files: the column, the paidAt labels in en, fr and es. The cli and pdf changes stay uncommitted in the working tree, and I won't use git stash to set them aside.
Action: Run git status, create the branch from here following the repo's branch naming (I'll ask the ticket number if needed), stage only the paid-at files, check git diff --cached, and commit.

Tabular numerals alone (tabular-nums) often stops digits jumping without a new font, but a monospace face works too if you want that look. JetBrains Mono needs to be loaded through the app's font setup.
Action: Find the invoice number and amount cells, apply a mono font stack with tabular-nums, right-align amounts, and check how it looks.

Doing items 1 and 3: pulling the empty state out of table.tsx into components/invoices/empty-state.tsx, and making the error state win over empty so a failed query no longer shows 'No invoices yet'. Tests are yours, and the other copy notes can wait.
Action: Move the empty state markup from table.tsx into the new component, reorder the checks around line 140 so isError renders first, and run typecheck.

I don't have a settled decision on me adding npm packages, so I can't say we agreed on something. Until you tell me otherwise I'll ask before adding any new dependency.
Action: Check the repo's contributing or docs pages for a dependency policy and tell you what's written.

I don't know the branch name offhand, so I'll find the editor store refactor branch first. The PR should mention the editor state going into a colocated zustand store, per ADR 0009.
Action: Check git branch and recent commits to confirm the branch, review its diff against origin/main, push it, and open the PR with gh using the repo's PR template.
